summary: Validated the EbxmlMustUnderstandInterceptor fix (iteration_27) with a REAL over-the-wire SOAP/HTTP round-trip — the exact test level that would have caught this bug in the first place (all prior tests called OrchestratorService.processInboundMessage() in-process, bypassing the CXF interceptor chain entirely). Wrote a new focus test EbxmlMustUnderstandInterceptorTest that (a) unit-verifies getUnderstoodHeaders() declares all 10 QNames in the OASIS ebMS_v2_0 msg-header-2_0.xsd namespace (4 emitted: MessageHeader/AckRequested/Acknowledgment/ErrorList + 6 defensive: SyncReply/TraceHeaderList/Via/MessageOrder/StatusRequest/StatusResponse), (b) publishes a real CXF JaxWsServerFactoryBean Provider<SOAPMessage> on a random localhost port using the Jetty HTTP transport (cxf-rt-transports-http-jetty, added as test-scope) and posts raw SOAP envelopes via java.net.http.HttpClient. Three real HTTP tests: (1) BUG REPRODUCTION — without the interceptor, CXF's built-in MustUnderstandEndingInterceptor throws SoapFault "MustUnderstand headers: [{...msg-header-2_0.xsd}MessageHeader] are not understood", HTTP 500 body contains that string, and Provider.invoke() is NEVER reached (proves the bug in the CXF phase chain). (2) FIX with just MessageHeader (mustUnderstand=1) — Provider.invoke() IS reached, response contains no 'not understood' fault. (3) FIX with MessageHeader + AckRequested both mustUnderstand=1 together (simulates an RM-profile message) — Provider.invoke() IS reached. All 4 assertions of this new class pass. Ran the full ebms-orchestrator Surefire suite: 35/35 tests pass, BUILD SUCCESS, zero regressions on the pre-existing 34 tests (OutboundMessageServiceRollbackTest, OrchestratorServiceAntiSpoofingTest, OrchestratorServiceRetryHeaderTest, OutboundSoapClientDynamicTrustTest, RawPayloadCaptureInterceptorTest, MessageStatusReconciliationSchedulerTest, ApplicationYamlSchemaPropertyTest, EbmsOrchestratorApplicationTests all green). The Testcontainers-based *IntegrationTest classes are still excluded from surefire (same environment limitation as iteration_25/26 — no Docker daemon in the sandbox) and are unrelated to this fix. Noted the pre-existing WARN mentioned by the reviewer: OutboundSoapClient logs 'CXF HTTPConduit niet beschikbaar - fallback timeout: not a proxy instance' (see OutboundSoapClientDynamicTrustTest output above) — non-fatal, out of scope for this iteration.

minor.issue: Pre-existing WARN '[OUTBOUND] mTLS-configuratie mislukt: not a proxy instance' / 'CXF HTTPConduit niet beschikbaar - fallback timeout: not a proxy instance' — non-fatal, falls back to default timeout. Explicitly out of scope for iteration_27 per reviewer note; flagged here only for tracking.

Optional: consider promoting cxf-rt-transports-http-jetty from test scope to a Spring Boot @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment=RANDOM_PORT) integration test once Docker becomes available in CI, so the full Spring/CxfEndpointConfig-driven registration path is also covered end-to-end (this iteration used a bare JaxWsServerFactoryBean to keep the test hermetic, but it exercises the exact same CXF interceptor chain including the built-in MustUnderstandEndingInterceptor, which is where the bug lived).
Optional (unrelated): fix the OutboundSoapClient 'not a proxy instance' WARN when getting HTTPConduit — reviewer explicitly deferred this.
critical_code_review_comments: EbxmlMustUnderstandInterceptor is minimal and correct: extends AbstractSoapInterceptor with Phase.READ, overrides getUnderstoodHeaders() to return an immutable Set.of(...) with exactly the 10 QNames requested by the reviewer, and both handleMessage()/handleFault() are documented no-ops. This is the idiomatic CXF pattern for declaring understood mustUnderstand headers — CXF's MustUnderstandEndingInterceptor iterates all inbound interceptors' getUnderstoodHeaders() and only faults on headers that no interceptor claims.

CxfEndpointConfig registration is on the single /ebms endpoint alongside RawPayloadCaptureInterceptor — covers ping/ack/regular inbound (all share the one endpoint per the app's design). Registration order after RawPayloadCaptureInterceptor is fine since the MustUnderstand check runs in Phase.PRE_LOGICAL and the getUnderstoodHeaders() contract is queried across ALL in-interceptors regardless of registration order.

The 6 defensive header declarations (SyncReply/TraceHeaderList/Via/MessageOrder/StatusRequest/StatusResponse) match the OASIS ebMS_v2_0 §3 header set and cost nothing at runtime — declaring them prevents future hard rejections if a compliant partner sends any of them with mustUnderstand=1, which our own SoapHelper doesn't do today.

Actual header PARSING is unchanged and still lives in SoapHelper.parseMessageHeader()/EbmsMessageProvider.invoke() — the interceptor is purely a CXF-contract declaration, no behavioural side-effects. This is exactly right; the previous code was correct in every respect EXCEPT for missing this one CXF-transport-layer declaration.

Test hygiene: the added cxf-rt-transports-http-jetty dependency is scope=test, so it is NOT shipped in the production fat-jar — the app in production keeps using the servlet-based transport via cxf-rt-transports-http (already present) inside Spring Boot's embedded Tomcat. Verified in pom.xml comment inline.

context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_27 fix (EbxmlMustUnderstandInterceptor) is validated by a real over-the-wire SOAP test that spins up a CXF Jetty HTTP endpoint on localhost and POSTs raw SOAP with mustUnderstand=1 ebXML headers. This is the FIRST test in this repo that exercises the actual CXF interceptor chain end-to-end (all prior tests are Mockito unit tests calling business methods directly). Before-fix behavior (BUG REPRO) is asserted in withoutInterceptor_realHttpPost_returnsMustUnderstandFault — the interceptor is disabled and the same SOAP envelope is rejected with the exact SoapFault the user saw in K8s. After-fix behavior is asserted in the two withInterceptor_* tests. cxf-rt-transports-http-jetty is added at test scope only, so no production artefact change. Testcontainers-based integration tests remain excluded (no Docker). Java 17, Maven 3.8.7, CXF 4.1.8, Spring Boot 3.4.1.
rca of the issue: Root cause: CXF's built-in MustUnderstandEndingInterceptor (phase POST_PROTOCOL, part of every CXF SOAP endpoint by default) collects the union of getUnderstoodHeaders() from all in-interceptors and, at the end of the READ chain, throws SoapFault 'MustUnderstand headers ... are not understood' for any SOAP header block with mustUnderstand="1" whose QName is NOT in that union. SoapHelper.buildOutboundSoap()/createAck() correctly set mustUnderstand=1 on the 4 emitted ebXML headers, and parseMessageHeader() correctly parses them — but nothing declared those header QNames as 'understood' to CXF at the transport level. Result: EVERY real inbound SOAP request over HTTP was rejected before EbmsMessageProvider.invoke() ran (100% rejection of production traffic in the user's K8s deployment). No existing test caught it because every test called OrchestratorService.processInboundMessage(...) directly, skipping the CXF phase chain entirely. Fix: new AbstractSoapInterceptor (EbxmlMustUnderstandInterceptor, Phase.READ, no-op handleMessage) with getUnderstoodHeaders() returning the 10 ebXML QNames, registered once on the /ebms endpoint in CxfEndpointConfig.ebmsEndpoint(...). Validation: EbxmlMustUnderstandInterceptorTest (a) proves bug reproduction on real HTTP without the interceptor (SoapFault + Provider never called) and (b) proves fix on real HTTP with the interceptor (no fault, Provider reached) — for both MessageHeader-only and MessageHeader+AckRequested payloads.
